'''Noah Hershkowitz''' (August 16, 1941 – November 13, 2020) was an American experimental plasma [[physicist]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hershkowitz, Noah - UW-Engineering Directory {{!}} College of Engineering @ The University of Wisconsin-Madison|url=https://directory.engr.wisc.edu/ep/faculty/hershkowitz_noah|access-date=2020-02-27|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Noah Hershkowitz Obituary - Madison, WI {{!}} Madison.com|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/madison/name/noah-hershkowitz-obituary?pid=197124530|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118181845/https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/madison/name/noah-hershkowitz-obituary?pid=197124530|archive-date=2020-11-18|access-date=2020-11-18|website=www.legacy.com}}</ref> He was known for his pioneering research on the understanding of [[Plasma sheath|plasma sheaths]], [[Soliton|solitons]] and [[Double layer (surface science)|double layers]] in plasmas,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hershkowitz|first1=Noah|last2=Romesser|first2=Thomas|date=1974|title=Observations of Ion-Acoustic Cylindrical Solitons|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=32|issue=11|pages=581–583|bibcode=1974PhRvL..32..581H|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.581}}</ref> as well as the development of the emissive probe which measures the plasma potential (i.e. the [[electric potential]] within a plasma sheath).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Smith|first1=J. R.|last2=Hershkowitz|first2=N.|last3=Coakley|first3=P.|date=1979-02-01|title=Inflection-point method of interpreting emissive probe characteristics|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.1135789|journal=Review of Scientific Instruments|volume=50|issue=2|pages=210–218|doi=10.1063/1.1135789|pmid=18699471|bibcode=1979RScI...50..210S |issn=0034-6748|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-11-15|title=Tribute to Prof. Noah Hershkowitz|url=https://mipse.umich.edu/news.php#hershkowitz|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118185533/https://mipse.umich.edu/news.php|archive-date=2020-11-18|access-date=2020-11-18|website=mipse.umich.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-09-26|title=Hershkowitz receives inaugural IEEE TPS award for plasma science research|url=https://www.engr.wisc.edu/news/hershkowitz-receives-inaugural-ieee-tps-award-plasma-science-research/|access-date=2020-11-18|website=College of Engineering - University of Wisconsin-Madison|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2004, Hershkowitz was co-awarded the 2004 [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for his contributions to the field of low-temperature plasmas.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=2004 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Hershkowitz&first_nm=Noah&year=2004|access-date=2020-02-27|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref> He was also awarded the 2015 [[IEEE Marie Sklodowska-Curie Award]] for his research and education of basic and applied plasma science.<ref name=":1" />

== Early life and career ==
Hershkowitz obtained a bachelor's degree from [[Union College]] in 1962 and a Ph.D. in physics from [[Johns Hopkins University]] in 1966. Upon graduation, Hershkowitz remained at the university to become an instructor in physics until 1967, where he was employed as assistant professor at the [[University of Iowa]] until 1980. During this time between 1974 and 1975, he was a visiting professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]]. Between 1980 and 1981, he was a visiting professor at the [[University of Colorado Boulder|University of Colorado, Boulder]]. In 1981, he became a professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]], and was the Irving Langmuir Professor of Engineering Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11601007.html|title=Hershkowitz, N. (Noah), 1941-|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-27}}</ref>

In 1992, Hershkowitz founded the journal ''[[Plasma Sources Science and Technology]]'' as the [[editor-in-chief]].<ref name=":2" />

== Scientific contributions ==
Hershkowitz' work on low temperature plasmas included [[RF heating|radio frequency wave heating]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Intrator|first1=T.|last2=Probert|first2=P. H.|last3=Vukovic|first3=M.|last4=Wukitch|first4=S.|last5=Elfimov|first5=A.|last6=Durst|first6=R.|last7=Breun|first7=R. A.|last8=Brouchous|first8=D.|last9=Diebold|first9=D.|last10=Doczy|first10=M.|last11=Fonck|first11=R.|date=1996|title=Alfvén ion–ion hybrid wave heating in the Phaedrus-T tokamak|url=http://digital.library.wisc.edu/1793/9834|journal=Physics of Plasmas|volume=3|issue=4|pages=1331–1339|bibcode=1996PhPl....3.1331I|doi=10.1063/1.871786|issn=1070-664X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sheehan|first1=J. P.|last2=Barnat|first2=E. V.|last3=Weatherford|first3=B. R.|last4=Kaganovich|first4=I. D.|last5=Hershkowitz|first5=N.|date=2014|title=Emissive sheath measurements in the afterglow of a radio frequency plasma|url=http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ef11/1b3ec7fa3eb58f4dafd2d4f3aa4662d34548.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190308214721/http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ef11/1b3ec7fa3eb58f4dafd2d4f3aa4662d34548.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=2019-03-08|journal=Physics of Plasmas|volume=21|issue=1|pages=013510|bibcode=2014PhPl...21a3510S|doi=10.1063/1.4861888|s2cid=16251078|issn=1070-664X}}</ref> [[Plasma sheath|sheath physics]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hershkowitz|first=Noah|date=2005|title=Sheaths: More complicated than you think|url=http://digital.library.wisc.edu/1793/8686|journal=Physics of Plasmas|volume=12|issue=5|pages=055502|bibcode=2005PhPl...12e5502H|doi=10.1063/1.1887189|issn=1070-664X|doi-access=free}}</ref> potential profiles,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hershkowitz|first=Noah|date=1985|title=Review of recent laboratory double layer experiments|journal=Space Science Reviews|language=en|volume=41|issue=3|pages=351–391|bibcode=1985SSRv...41..351H|doi=10.1007/BF00190655|s2cid=120426051|issn=1572-9672}}</ref> [[Plasma diagnostics|diagnostic probes]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Smith|first1=J. R.|last2=Hershkowitz|first2=N.|last3=Coakley|first3=P.|date=1979|title=Inflection-point method of interpreting emissive probe characteristics|journal=Review of Scientific Instruments|volume=50|issue=2|pages=210–218|bibcode=1979RScI...50..210S|doi=10.1063/1.1135789|issn=0034-6748|pmid=18699471}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Koo|first1=Bon-Woong|last2=Hershkowitz|first2=Noah|last3=Sarfaty|first3=Moshe|date=1999|title=Langmuir probe in low temperature, magnetized plasmas: Theory and experimental verification|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|volume=86|issue=3|pages=1213–1220|bibcode=1999JAP....86.1213K|doi=10.1063/1.370873|issn=0021-8979}}</ref> and the industrial applications of plasmas.

Hershkowitz became director of the [[Phaedrus Tandem Mirror]] experiment at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1980. The group made contributions in demonstrating the stability of RF (radio frequency) heating in magnetic confinement devices.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Severn |first=Greg |last2=Baalrud |first2=Scott D. |last3=Foster |first3=John |date=2025-07-01 |title=Noah Hershkowitz: Experimental plasma physics pioneer |url=https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0267508 |journal=Physics of Plasmas |volume=32 |issue=7 |pages=070501 |doi=10.1063/5.0267508 |issn=1070-664X|doi-access=free }}</ref>

His work also has applications in [[magnetic confinement fusion]] (e.g. tokamaks, magnetic mirrors).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Intrator|first1=T.|last2=Probert|first2=P.|last3=Wukitch|first3=S.|last4=Vukovic|first4=M.|last5=Brouchous|first5=D.|last6=Diebold|first6=D.|last7=Breun|first7=R.|last8=Doczy|first8=M.|last9=Edgell|first9=D.|last10=Elfimov|first10=A.|last11=Hershkowitz|first11=N.|date=1995|title=Alfvén wave current drive in the Phaedrus-T tokamak|url=http://digital.library.wisc.edu/1793/9388|journal=Physics of Plasmas|volume=2|issue=6|pages=2263–2271|bibcode=1995PhPl....2.2263I|doi=10.1063/1.871249|issn=1070-664X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hatakeyama|first1=R.|last2=Hershkowitz|first2=N.|last3=Majeski|first3=R.|last4=Wen|first4=Y. J.|last5=Brouchous|first5=D. B.|last6=Proberts|first6=P.|last7=Breun|first7=R. A.|last8=Roberts|first8=D.|last9=Vukovic|first9=M.|last10=Tanaka|first10=T.|date=1997|title=Measurements on rotating ion cyclotron range of frequencies induced particle fluxes in axisymmetric mirror plasmas|url=http://digital.library.wisc.edu/1793/8694|journal=Physics of Plasmas|volume=4|issue=8|pages=2947–2954|bibcode=1997PhPl....4.2947H|doi=10.1063/1.872427|issn=1070-664X}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Hershkowitz has been a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] since 1981. 

In 2004, Hershkowitz was jointly awarded the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] with [[Valery Godyak]] for his research on low-temperature plasmas.<ref name=":0" /> That same year he received the Plasma Prize of the [[American Vacuum Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plasma Science & Technology Division Plasma Prize |url=https://avs.org/awards/division-group-awards/plasma-science-technology-division-plasma-prize/ |access-date=26 January 2024 |website=American Vacuum Society}}</ref> In 2015, he received the [[IEEE Marie Sklodowska-Curie Award]] for "''innovative research and inspiring education in basic and applied plasma science''".<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=IEEE Marie Sklodowska-Curie Award|url=https://www.ieee.org/about/awards/technical-field-awards/curie.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001164346/https://www.ieee.org/about/awards/technical-field-awards/curie.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 1, 2019|access-date=2020-11-18|website=[[IEEE]]}}</ref>
